title: When a celebration must contain everything

captions.energy: Demanding the whole plan be fulfilled

meaning: The pleasure you create can become restrictive when the evening must contain every idea and justify each preparation.
text: Generously prepared leisure can acquire too many conditions. The Empress in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps make enjoyment real: choosing treats, imagining activities and collecting pleasant details. The World in energy leans towards demanding complete fulfilment of the design, as though one missing part would spoil the whole. The Devil in emotions shows attachment to promised enjoyment. Releasing something already given so much anticipation becomes difficult. Creating, seeking completeness and feeling bound have distinct roles; the more you prepare, the more important freedom to choose together remains.

For example, you plan a board game, a homemade dessert and an old comedy. The first game runs long, and an enjoyable conversation takes another half hour. **Shared pleasure need not complete the entire list.** You can leave the comedy for another day while keeping delight in what already happened. Prepared variety remains a supply of possibilities, instead of becoming a timetable you must both satisfy regardless of desire.

The difficulty is experiencing a missed activity as the loss of all fullness. You hurry the conversation, finish the game without interest and watch the film from an obligation to fit it in. The promised celebration holds more tightly than living enjoyment. Trying to preserve the whole plan drains each moment. Permission to finish at a pleasant point keeps leisure a choice you share, even when the plan exceeded the available time.
